summary: No held thesis is broken on fundamentals. Nothing in close.json or the news memory shows a guidance cut, a negative 8-K, a 4.01/4.02 or a menu drop for any of the 13 held names. Today's moves (EXEL -1.2% on its first day, DPZ +2.3%, KR +1.4%) are one day of price, not evidence. Today's trades left the quality cases intact. EXEL (F7, gp_sector_pct 0.935, CFO $884.3M against net income $782.6M) was bought at $69.04. KR (CFO $7.31B against net income $1.02B, but F7 with failed roa_improved and current_ratio_improved) was added at $70.20. The WMT trim filled at $127.58, and WMT still passes the screen (F7, 0.865). MSCI's restated thesis closes the 11-12 L3/L6 flag. The weakest cash backing among held names is still FAST (CFO about 1.03x net income), which is thin but not a break. No lesson in learning.json names the Fundamentals Analyst in applies_to. I used L3 and L6 as checks because past Fundamentals reviews supplied their evidence. I have no graded calls yet.
update: Two stored texts written today break L6 and should be restated through thesis_updates tomorrow. (1) EXEL's invalidation says $65 is 'about 9.4% under the $71.74 menu close of 11-10'. (2) KR's invalidation measures $61.50 from the 10-22 fill and 'the $69.81 mark on 11-13', not from the blended cost of the two lots in close.json. Things to watch: EXEL's invalidation includes 'the fundamentals screen drops EXEL from the menu', so tomorrow's morning run must check that clause in fundamentals.json, along with any held name that falls into holdings_not_on_menu. EXEL and VRSN both rest on annual figures that predate their Q3 prints (10-29 and 10-22), so treat their ranks as stale until a newer fiscal year appears. The oncology pair (INCY 2.4% plus EXEL 2.4%) is about 4.8% of equity, just under the PM's 5% line, and single-name trial risk now sits behind two names. Under L3, DPZ (11.1%), WMT (8.1%) and KR (5.9%) are still about 25% of equity in 'Consumer Staples' by SIC label. The trim and the KR add lowered the bucket figure but left the label stack about flat, and DPZ's Staples rank remains a wholesale-groceries artifact. WMT's 11-19 print is the only near-term event that could break a held fundamental thesis through its guidance-cut clause.
